info.description:
Overview

This Postman collection provides a curated set of APIs that we recommend you explore as part of your integration with the 1Kosmos platform. These APIs are designed to help you quickly evaluate key features and capabilities, such as identity verification, authentication, and user management.

Whether you're building a POC or testing specific functionality, this collection offers a simplified, ready-to-use starting point. Each request includes pre-filled sample data and descriptions to help you understand the request/response structure and expected behavior.

item.name: Set up

request.description:
This API is used to fetch the complete details of both the tenant and the community that were set as the environment variables.

These details include configured tenant dns name and the list of other tenant DNS. Additionally, the community details include the logo URL used in the community, tenant tag, and so on. The logo details will be displayed only if you had set the skipLogos parameter in the payload to false.

Mandatory Parmameters

  • dns - Use the dns name of the tenant as a variable.

  • communityName - Specify the community name as a variable.

Optional Parameters

skipLogos - This is a boolean parameter. Specifying this value as false displays the logo details in the response.

This API is used to retrieve all microservices associated with your tenant. You must execute this API to know the URLs of each services. For example, if service A want to call service B, it is necessary for service A to know the URL for service B.

item.description:
Before you begin to execute APIs, you must set up your community and tenant information in your Environments.

Use the Get tenant community Info API to fetch the community information.

To set up your environment, follow these steps:

  1. Use the Get tenant community Info API to fetch the community information.

  2. Navigate to the Environments menu and click +. The New Environment page is displayed.

2. In the Variable column, add the following parameters in the same format:

  • tenantDNS

  • community_name

  • licensekey

Note: The above parameters are case sensitive.

3. In the Type column, specify the value as default for all the three parameters.

4. In the Initial value column, specify the following values for each parameter:

  • tenantDNS - Specify your tenant name.

  • community_name - Specify your community name.

  • licensekey - Specify the license key of your tenant.

5. In the Current value column, specify the same value as that of the initial value for all the three parameters.

item.description:
ID Verification is a service designed by 1Kosmos to verify user identity documents such as driver's licenses, passports, and national ID cards. 1Kosmos analyzes document data under stringent security protocols, prioritizing high data safety standards to protect user data.

How 1Kosmos ID Verification helps:

  • 1Kosmos ID Verification simplifies the identity verification process for new users by validating their information through government-issued IDs, face liveness checks & face comparison.

  • 1Kosmos ID Verification performs single-source KYC and anti-money laundering verification, delivering a one-stop compliance solution for both customers and developers.

How It Works

  • Users initiate a verification session for users, specifying the document type.

  • Users complete the verification process, which involves document validation and selfie verification.

  • Once the verification is complete, the API response provides session details, including status and validation results.

  • If the verification is successful, the session details are returned in the response.

  • If the verification fails, the API returns an error code, and the verification status is marked as NOT PERFORMED or FAILED.

Session URL Validity

  • By default, the generated session URL is valid for 7 days.

  • dvcID* parameter can be adjust to modify session URL's validity period as per your need. Please contact your 1Kosmos representative further information.

This API ensures secure and efficient document verification for identity validation across multiple platforms.

* dvcID refers to the specific type of verification workflow a user must complete. Examples of verification workflows include:
1. Document + selfie verification
2. Document verification only
3. Document verification + document issuing authority verification

item.description:
Fetch IAL of a User

Identity Assurance Levels (IALs) are a set of standards defined by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) that convey the degree of confidence that someone's claimed identity is their real identity.

1Kosmos supports the following Identity Assurance Levels:

  • IAL1: No requirement to link the individual to a specific real-life identity. Any information provided by the individual should be treated as self-asserted.

  • IAL2: Uses digital documents to support the real-world existence of an identity and verifies that the correct person is associated with it.

In 1Kosmos, IAL is calculated when

  • a user enrolls an identity document

  • a user unenrolls an identity document

  • an authorized party inspects IAL for a user

Here’s how a user can be certified from IAL1 to IAL2:

  • If both their driving license and passport have been verified.

  • If their SSN is verified, but neither their passport nor driving license is verified.

  • If neither the driving license nor the passport is verified.

item.name: Reports

request.description:
API Request Description

This endpoint allows you to retrieve event data for a specific community within a tenant.

Request URL

POST {{client_api}}/reports/tenant/:tenantID/community/:communityID/events

Request Parameters

  • pSize (integer): The number of records to return per page. In the example, it is set to 10.

  • pIndex (integer): The page index for pagination. In the example, it is set to 1.

  • from (string): The start date and time for the events to be retrieved, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.SSS. In the example, it is 2025-05-01 00:00:00.000.

  • to (string): The end date and time for the events to be retrieved, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.SSS. In the example, it is 2025-05-10 00:00:00.000.

  • query (object): An object containing the search criteria for the events. In the example, it includes:

    • event_name (string): The name of the event to filter by. In the example, it is set to "E_IDV_DOCUMENT_VALIDATE".

Expected Response

  • Status Code: 200 OK

  • Content-Type: application/json

  • Response Body:

    • page (object): Contains pagination information.

      • total (integer): Total number of records available.

      • pSize (integer): The size of the current page.

      • pIndex (integer): The current page index.

    • data (array): An array of event data objects. If no events are found, this will be an empty array.

Example Response

{
  "page": {
    "total": 0,
    "pSize": 0,
    "pIndex": 0
  },
  "data": []
}

Notes

  • Ensure that you provide valid tenantID and communityID in the URL.

  • The request requires authorization headers which must be included for successful execution.

  • The response may vary based on the provided date range and query parameters.

request.description:
Request Description

This API endpoint is used to submit metrics data for a specific community within a tenant. The purpose of this request is to track and analyze various metrics related to community activities.

Request Parameters

The request must include a JSON body with the following parameters:

  • metricsName (string): The name of the metric you want to report (e.g., "M_GT_SUCCESSFUL_AUTHENTICATION").

  • from (string): The start date and time for the metric data in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.sss.

  • to (string): The end date and time for the metric data in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.sss.

Response Structure

The API responds with a JSON object containing the following field:

  • count (integer): The number of records that match the provided metrics criteria. For example, a response of {"count":0} indicates that there were no records found for the specified metrics within the given date range.

Example Request

{
  "metricsName": "M_GT_SUCCESSFUL_AUTHENTICATION",
  "from": "2025-05-01 00:00:00.000",
  "to": "2025-05-01 00:00:00.000"
}

Example Response

{
  "count": 0
}

request.description:
Request Description

This API endpoint allows you to generate an application usage report for a specific tenant and community within the client application.

Request Method

  • POST

Request URL

  • {{client_api}}/reports/tenant/:tenantID/community/:communityID/application_usage_report

Request Body

The request body must be in JSON format and should contain the following parameters:

  • from (string): The start date and time for the report in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss.SSS.

  • to (string): The end date and time for the report in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss.SSS.

  • pSize (integer): The number of records to return per page.

  • pIndex (integer): The index of the page to return.

Example Payload:

{
  "from": "2025-05-01 00:00:00.000",
  "to": "2026-06-01 00:00:00.000",
  "pSize": 10,
  "pIndex": 0
}

Expected Response

The response will be a JSON object containing:

  • page: An object with pagination details.

    • total (integer): The total number of records available.

    • pSize (integer): The number of records per page.

    • pIndex (integer): The current page index.

  • data: An array of objects representing the application usage events. Each object may include fields such as:

    • event_name (string): The name of the event.

    • event_ts (integer): The timestamp of the event.

    • user_id (string): The ID of the user associated with the event.

    • Additional fields related to the event and user details.

Example Response:

{
  "page": {
    "total": 0,
    "pSize": 0,
    "pIndex": 0
  },
  "data": []
}

Notes

  • Ensure that the tenantID and communityID in the URL are replaced with valid identifiers.

  • The request requires appropriate authorization headers to be included.

  • The response may vary based on the data available for the specified time range.

request.description:
Passwordless Login Activity Report Request

This request is used to retrieve a report on passwordless login activities for a specific tenant and community. It allows the user to specify a date range and an event name to filter the results.

Request URL

POST {{client_api}}/reports/tenant/:tenantID/community/:communityID/passwordless_login_activity_report

Request Body

The request body must be in JSON format and includes the following parameters:

  • pSize (number): The number of records to return per page.

  • pIndex (number): The index of the page to return.

  • from (string): The start date and time for the report in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.SSS.

  • to (string): The end date and time for the report in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.SSS.

  • eventName (string): The name of the event to filter the report.

Example Request Body
{
  "pSize": 10,
  "pIndex": 0,
  "from": "2025-05-01 00:00:00.000",
  "to": "2026-06-01 00:00:00.000",
  "eventName": "E_SP_REDIRECT_SUCCEEDED"
}

Response Structure

The response will be in JSON format and contains the following structure:

  • page: An object that provides pagination information.

    • total (number): The total number of records available.

    • pSize (number): The size of the page.

    • pIndex (number): The index of the current page.

  • data: An array of objects, each representing a login event with the following fields:

    • event_name (string): The name of the event.

    • event_ts (number): The timestamp of the event.

    • version (string): The version of the event.

    • journey_id (string): The ID of the user journey.

    • session_id (string): The ID of the session.

    • client_ip_address (string): The IP address of the client.

    • caller_user_agent (string): The user agent of the caller.

    • user_id (string): The ID of the user.

    • user_status (string): The status of the user.

    • user_email (string): The email of the user.

    • user_firstname (string): The first name of the user.

    • user_lastname (string): The last name of the user.

    • source_user_directory (string): The source user directory.

    • source_user_directory_name (string): The name of the source user directory.

    • caller_ip (string): The IP address of the caller.

    • tenant_dns (string): The DNS of the tenant.

    • auth_method (string): The authentication method used.

    • auth_device_os (string): The operating system of the device used for authentication.

    • auth_device_app_name (string): The name of the application used for authentication.

    • auth_device_app_version (string): The version of the application used for authentication.

    • sp_type (string): The type of service provider.

    • sp_name (string): The name of the service provider.

    • sp_id (string): The ID of the service provider.

    • country (string): The country of the user.

    • region (string): The region of the user.

    • tenant_id (string): The ID of the tenant.

    • community_id (string): The ID of the community.

    • type (string): The type of event.

    • authJourneysMatched (array): An array of matched authentication journeys, each containing:

      • id (string): The ID of the journey.

      • name (string): The name of the journey.

    • aliasUsed (string): The alias used for the event.

    • event_id (string): The ID of the event.

    • timestamp (string): The timestamp of the event.

    • epoch_time (number): The epoch time of the event.

    • eventName (string): The name of the event.

This structure allows for detailed reporting on passwordless login activities, enabling analysis and insights into user interactions.

This endpoint generates a One-Time Password (OTP) for a specified user within a community. The OTP can be sent via SMS based on the provided parameters.

Request

Method: POST

Request Body

The request body must be in JSON format and should include the following parameters:

Field Name Required Field Type Description
userId Yes string The unique identifier of the user. It can be User's ID or UUID or any other transaction ID
communityId Yes string The identifier of the community associated with the user.
tenantId Yes string The identifier for the tenant in which the user exists.
smsTo Yes string The recipient's phone number for OTP via SMS.
smsISDCode Yes string The International Subscriber Dialing code for the SMS.
smsFrom No string The identifier for the source of the SMS.
smsTemplateB64 No string A base64 encoded template for the SMS message.
smsTemplateId No string The identifier for the SMS template.
trace No boolean A flag to enable or disable tracing for the request.
validitySeconds No integer OTP expiration Time
serviceName No string Name of the service for which OTP was generated

Response

The response will return a status code indicating the result of the OTP generation request.

  • Status Code: 202 (Accepted)

  • Content-Type: application/json

  • Response Body:

    • messageId (string): An identifier for the message sent. In this case, it may be empty.

    • info (string): Additional information about the request. This may also be empty.

  • Ensure that all parameters are provided correctly to avoid errors.

  • A 202 status code indicates that the request has been accepted for processing, but the processing is not yet complete.

This endpoint is used to verify a One-Time Password (OTP) submitted by a user during the authentication process. It ensures that the provided OTP corresponds to the user and is valid for the specified community and tenant.

Field Name Required Field Type Description
code Yes string The OTP code that the user has received and is attempting to verify.
userId Yes string The same unique identifier used to generate the OTP.
userPublicKey No string The public key associated with the user, used for cryptographic verification.
communityId Yes string The identifier for the community to which the user belongs.
tenantId Yes string The identifier for the tenant associated with the community.
serviceName No string Name of the service for which OTP is being verified

Field Name Type Description
error_code integer A code representing the status of the request. A value of 0 typically indicates no error.
message string A message providing additional information about the request status. This may be empty or contain relevant info.
status boolean Indicates whether the OTP verification was successful or not.

{
  "error_code": 0,
  "message": "",
  "status": true
}

HTTP Status Error Message Description
403 OTP request locked for the user. Too many wrong OTPs & tries a new OTP
410 OTP match found, but the validity time has expired Expired OTP
404 Invalid OTP Wrong OTP
400 Unable to load tenant/community Incorrect tenant/community
409 OTP already used OTP already used

  • Ensure that the OTP code is valid and has not expired before making the request.

  • The response may vary based on the success or failure of the verification process.

This endpoint allows you to fetch user details from a specified community within a tenant. It is particularly useful for retrieving user information based on specific query parameters.

HTTP Method

POST

Endpoint

{{client_api}}/users-mgmt/tenant/tenantId/community/communityId/users/fetch

Request Parameters

The request body must be in JSON format and includes the following parameters:

  • authModule (string): A unique identifier for the authentication module being used.

  • pIndex (integer): The index of the page to be retrieved, starting from 0.

  • pSize (integer): The number of records to return per page.

  • query (object): An object containing the search criteria. In this case, it includes:

    • username (string): The username of the user to be searched.

  • attributes (array of strings): An array specifying which attributes to include in the response. Using ["\\\*"] requests all available attributes.

Expected Response Format

The response will be in JSON format and will include the following structure:

  • page (object): Contains pagination information.

    • index (integer): The current page index.

    • total (integer): The total number of records available.

    • size (integer): The number of records returned in this response.

  • data (array): An array of user objects matching the query. Each user object may contain:

    • username (string): The username of the user.

    • uid (string): The unique identifier for the user.

    • dguid (string): The directory GUID for the user.

    • disabled (boolean): Indicates if the user account is disabled.

    • status (string): The current status of the user.

    • roleValue (string): The role assigned to the user.

    • type (string): The type of user.

    • moduleId (string): The module ID associated with the user.

    • lastname (string): The last name of the user.

    • email (string): The email address of the user.

    • urn (string): The uniform resource name associated with the user.

  • publicKey (string): A public key for security purposes.

  • signature_token (string): A token used for signature verification.

item.description:
These APIs are used to initiate and manage an ID verification (IDV) session for an end user. They enable creation of a workflow instance to start the verification process and allow polling of the session status to retrieve the final result upon completion.

Envionment setup:

Before you begin to execute APIs, you must set up your community and tenant information in your Environments.

To set up your environment, follow these steps:

  • Navigate to the Environments menu and click +. The New Environment page is displayed.

2. In the Variable column, add the following parameters in the same format:

  • client_api

  • my_public_key

  • my_private_key

  • licenseKey

  • client_community_name

Note: The above parameters are case sensitive.

3. In the Type column, specify the value as default for all the three parameters.

4. In the Initial value column, specify the following values for each parameter:

  • client_api - Specify your tenant URL (For Example: https://acme.1kosmos.net)

  • my_public_key - Your ECDSA Public Key

  • my_private_key - Your ECDSA Private Key

  • client_community_name - Specify your community name.

  • licenseKey - Specify the license key of your tenant.

5. In the Current value column, specify the same value as that of the initial value for all the three parameters.

Required Details for the Create Workflow Instance API

  • workflowId (Required): Workflow ID provided during provisioning

  • metaData.firstName (Recommended): Used for name matching

  • metaData.lastName (Recommended): Used for name matching

  • metaData.dob (Recommended): Format YYYY-MM-DD, used for DOB matching

  • metaData.email (Optional): Informational

  • metaData.callbackUrl (Recommended): Redirect URL after session completion

Workflow Status Values

The workflow instance progresses through the following statuses:

  • pending - The session has been created but has not yet been started.

  • started - The session has been initiated and verification is in progress.

  • completed - The verification process has finished and the result is available.

  • expired - The session has timed out before completion.

  • failed - The verification process did not succeed.
